steps.title: Digital vs Analog
steps.markdownContent:
Electronic signals talk to the Arduino in two different ways:

### 1. Digital Signals: Two Clear Choices 💡
Digital is like a standard light switch. It is either completely **ON** or completely **OFF**:
- **HIGH**: Full power (+5 Volts) ➔ ON!
- **LOW**: Zero power (0 Volts) ➔ OFF!
There is no halfway state in digital logic.

### 2. Analog Signals: A Smooth Slide 🎚️
Analog is like a volume dial or dimmer slider. It can be any smooth value along a range:
- Whisper quiet, medium sound, or full blast!
- Nighttime dark, twilight, or blazing sunshine!

On the Arduino, analog inputs measure voltages smoothly from **0 all the way to 1023**.

Let's explore how the Arduino handles these two different types of signals!

quickCheck.question: A standard light switch is either flipped ON or flipped OFF. Is this digital or analog?
quickCheck.explanation: Digital signals have only two states (ON or OFF), just like a regular light switch!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Digital means two simple choices: ON or OFF, HIGH or LOW. Think of a simple light switch.

quickCheck.question: A volume knob turns smoothly from whisper-quiet to super loud. Is that digital or analog?
quickCheck.explanation: Because the volume changes smoothly through many levels in between, it is an analog signal!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Analog signals can be any level in between, like sliding a volume bar up and down.

steps.title: HIGH/LOW vs. Continuous Waves
steps.markdownContent:
### Visualizing Digital vs. Analog Signals 📈

Look at how these two signals appear on an engineer's oscilloscope screen:

```
DIGITAL SIGNAL (Square Wave)
+5V (HIGH) ──┐        ┌────────┐
             │        │        │
 0V (LOW)    └────────┘        └────────> Time
             Only 2 States: ON or OFF!

ANALOG SIGNAL (Continuous Wave)
+5V          /\        .-.
            /  \      /   \
           /    \    /     \
 0V ──────'      '--'       '───────────> Time
     Infinite Smooth Values from 0 to 1023!
```

#### Why Both Matter in Robotics:
| Signal Type | Arduino Voltage Range | Numerical Value in Code | Everyday Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Digital** | 0V or 5V | `LOW` (0) or `HIGH` (1) | Light switch, push button, coin slot |
| **Analog** | 0.0V to 5.0V | `0` to `1023` (10-bit ADC) | Volume knob, thermometer, light sensor |

> **Pro Tip**: The Arduino has a special translator called an **ADC** (Analog-to-Digital Converter) that slices smooth voltages from 0V to 5V into 1,024 tiny stair-steps (0 to 1023)!

steps.title: Interactive Signal Inspector & Prediction
steps.markdownContent:
### Flip the Switch & Turn the Dial! 🎛️

Use the interactive inspector below to test both signal worlds:
1. **Digital Switch (Pin 13)**: Flip between `LOW` (0.0V) and `HIGH` (5.0V). Notice there is no middle ground!
2. **Analog Slider (Pin A0)**: Slide the voltage smoothly from 0.0V up to 5.0V and observe the raw reading change from `0` to `1023`.
3. **Engineering Prediction**: Predict what happens to the sensor reading as a knob rotates smoothly!

interactiveConfig.question: What voltage does HIGH represent on a standard 5V Arduino Uno digital pin?
interactiveConfig.explanation: On a 5V Arduino Uno, HIGH connects the pin to full positive supply voltage (+5V).

questions.question: What voltage does HIGH represent on a standard 5V Arduino Uno digital pin?
questions.explanation: On a 5V Arduino Uno, HIGH connects the pin to full positive supply voltage (+5V).

questions.question: What is the numerical range of numbers an Arduino analog input pin reads?
questions.explanation: The Uno's 10-bit analog converter divides voltages between 0V and 5V into 1024 discrete steps (0 through 1023).

questions.question: A light sensor detects daylight gradually changing from morning sunrise to noon. Is this signal digital or analog?
questions.explanation: Because brightness increases smoothly throughout the morning, it is an analog signal!
